title: probabilistic-acceptance-windows-for-batching-and-cache-recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a regression-detection and safe-apply system for automated batching/caching recommendations. Instead of a single hard threshold, use probabilistic acceptance windows that combine micro-benchmarks, canary prompt corpus comparisons, and semantic-fidelity drift detectors to decide whether to apply, hold, or rollback configuration changes. The feature should integrate with the existing recommenders (batching advisor and cache tuner) and the rollout orchestration pipeline to enable staged applies with automatic rollback on quality regressions or downstream latency deviations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New config recommendations from the cost recommender can be applied via a staged rollout that uses a probabilistic acceptance window rather than a single pass/fail metric

A2: The system runs a lightweight canary evaluation set ("canary-corpus") on 0.5-5% of live traffic during staged rollout and reports semantic-fidelity metrics (BLEU-like, embedding-similarity, and task-specific success) in the Console

A3: Rollback triggers are defined and tested: 95% posterior probability that quality has degraded beyond the acceptance window OR latency tail SLO violation observed for two consecutive epochs triggers automatic rollback
A4: Dashboard shows per-config delta in cost/tokens, delta in quality metrics, confidence intervals, and a link to the failing prompt examples
A5: Integration tests validate that when the canary-corpus exhibits an induced regression, the orchestrator halts and rolls back the change within the configured rollback window
implementation_steps: 1) Define probabilistic acceptance model: choose priors, metric mix, and decision rules (Maya + Diego)
2) Create canary-corpus generator: sampling policy and synthetic augmentation to cover edge-cases (Priya)
3) Extend recommender output schema with risk score, expected token-savings distribution, and suggested rollout plan
4) Implement lightweight canary runner to evaluate candidate config against baseline on small fraction of live traffic
5) Add drift detectors: embedding-similarity delta, output entropy shift, and task-specific KPIs
6) Wire rollouts: staged percentages, escalation windows, automatic rollback hooks
7) Console UX: acceptance window visualization and incident links
8) Add end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (induce model regression, simulate infra noise)
9) Run internal pilot on non-critical customer namespace and analyze results
10) Gradual opt-in rollout and documentation + runbook for on-call
test_plan: Unit tests for probabilistic decision function with synthetic distributions
Simulation harness: run thousands of synthetic candidate recommendations and verify false-positive/negative rates are within SLA
Canary evaluation: compare outputs for known-good and known-bad candidate configs using the canary-corpus
A/B live test on staging: 2% traffic with induced latency bump to validate rollback triggers
Post-rollback forensic job that captures failing traces and stores them for triage
monitoring: Console: per-recommendation summary (expected savings, observed savings, quality delta, confidence interval)
Alert: auto-rollback executed (pager to on-call) when rollback condition met
Metric: false-positive rate and rollback frequency tracked per-week
SLOs: maintain 99.9% availability during staged rollouts and <0.5% of canary-triggered wrong rollbacks week-over-week
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive batching reduces per-token context fidelity. Mitigation: conservative prior and lower initial scale factor; require stronger evidence to expand batch sizes.
Risk: Canary corpus not representative. Mitigation: automated corpus refresh and stratified sampling from production examples plus synthetic edge cases.
Risk: Metric noise causing spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: use Bayesian smoothing and require sustained signal across multiple evaluation epochs before rollback.
Risk: Performance regressions from environment noise. Mitigation: correlate with infra metrics (GPU util, kernel failures) before deciding rollback due to latency
